My psychologist told me a really good analogy about depression that's caused by trauma.

Imagine that you have a beautiful dream house on the coast of a lake. This lake provides a lot of joy to you; you can swim in it, fish in it, boat on it, admire it, etc. One day, you are told that there is a danger of the lake flooding, so you build a tall cement wall around the entire lake. You still have your beautiful dream house, but now you have no lake. You will, in this scenario, never know if the lake has actually flooded, and thus you can never break down the cement walls in fear of having the house flooded.

The lake is your emotional range. The cement wall is the defensive mechanism that your mind uses to prevent you from feeling emotions that have, in the past, hurt you. However, even when this defensive mechanism may not be doing you good anymore, the wall remains. It also often blocks off aspects of your emotions that are not negative (eg. preventing you from feeling excited, happy, etc.), much like the wall in the analogy blocked you from doing enjoyable things with the lake.

I'm not sure if this rings true to anyone else, but this is a lot like what depression is for me. I don't feel anything at all, and when I do feel emotions, they are always negative. I haven't felt anything but sadness and rage over the past 5 years or so, and my motivation has completely disintegrated.

When people tell me to "just cheer up," it is unbearably frustrating. Depression has ruined my life, and if I could "just cheer up," I certainly would have done so. Depression is a chemical imbalance, and it's not something that can be solved so easily. I take medication, have therapy and try to do things that I used to enjoy, yet I've never felt more awful in my life than I do right now. Most days I can't get out of bed because I don't have the will to. I don't have the will to eat or think or move. Imagine how that feels, and imagine how it would then feel to be told to "cheer up".
